title: Empirical Phenomenology: Action as Disclosure and the Science of Opaque Public Systems
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
A methodological foundation for studying opaque public systems through their observable effects. Its founding principle is that action does not make an actor fully knowable but makes total unknowability impossible: causal intervention leaves nonzero inferential signal in the structure of its outcomes.

The paper applies this principle to generative search systems whose internal models, ranking functions, safety layers, and version histories are inaccessible. It treats external behavioral observation as a proper science rather than a provisional substitute for internal access, subsumes the archive’s earlier immanent phenomenology as one technique, and grounds ECS, CDI, Drowning Test, PER, and traversal logging as instruments for dated, comparative, longitudinal study.
